title: Protocol for engineering and validating a synthetic mitochondrial intermembrane bridge in mammalian cells
protocol: Clean workbench, pipettes, and vial stands with RNaseZap reagent before starting RNA isolation.
Harvest 5 million cells/sample as per standard cell harvesting protocol.
Add TRIzol reagent to the cell pellet (1 mL per 5 × 10^6 cells).
Homogenize cells by vigorous pipetting 10 times.
Add 0.2 mL chloroform to the homogenized cell suspension.
Shake tube vigorously or vortex for 15 seconds and incubate at room temperature for 2–3 minutes.
Centrifuge at 12,000 g for 15 minutes at 4°C.
Aspirate the upper, colorless aqueous phase into a separate vial.
Be very careful when removing the upper layer; do not aspirate or disturb the middle white ring-like layer.
Aspirate approximately 400 μL of aqueous phase.
Add 280 μL of isopropanol and mix by gently inverting the tube.
Incubate for 10 min at room temperature (20°C–22°C).
Centrifuge at 12,000 g for 30 min at 4°C.
Carefully remove the supernatant.
Wash the pellet twice with 1 mL of 75% ethanol by centrifuging at 7,500 g for 5 min at 4°C.
Remove the supernatant completely after washing.
Air dry the pellet for 5 min at room temperature (20°C–22°C).
Dissolve RNA in 30 μL of RNase-free water by gentle pipetting and incubate for 5 min at 55°C.
Incubate RNA-primer mix for 5 min at 65°C.
Place RNA-primer mix on ice for 1 min immediately after incubation.
Vortex and briefly centrifuge 5× SSIV reverse transcriptase buffer before proceeding.
Heat PCR machine to 50°C.
Heat water bath or heat block to 80°C.
Prepare reverse transcriptase mix by adding 4 μL of 5× SSIV buffer, 1 μL 100 mM DTT, 1 μL ribonuclease inhibitor, and 1 μL SSIV reverse transcriptase enzyme.
Handle DTT with caution and store it in small aliquots at -20°C.
Add freshly prepared reverse transcriptase mix to RNA-primer mix.
Incubate the combined reaction mixture for 10 min at 50°C.
Heat-inactivate the reverse transcriptase by incubating for 10 min at 80°C.
Add 2 units of RNase H and incubate for 20 min at 37°C.
Use 10 ng of cDNA and the primers Fwd BamHI-SCO1 and Rev SCO1-LacI.
Follow the protocol provided by Phusion Hot Start II High-Fidelity PCR Master Mix with 68°C setting for annealing temperature.
Separate samples on a 1% agarose gel.
Observe ethidium bromide-stained relevant DNA bands under a transilluminator.
Cut out the 370 bp-fragment from the gel.
Use a fresh scalpel/blade for gel cutting.
Protect eyes and body during UV exposure.
Make cuts around the amplified band under the transilluminator.
Switch off the transilluminator after making cuts.
Purify the amplicon by following the gel extraction protocol as per kit manual.
Use 10 ng of cDNA with primers Fwd LacI-TOMM20 and Rev TOMM20-His-EcoRI.
Follow Phusion Hot Start II High-Fidelity PCR Master Mix protocol at 68°C for annealing.
Separate the samples on a 1.5% agarose gel after PCR amplification.
Observe relevant DNA bands under a transilluminator.
Excise the 115-bp fragment from the gel.
Purify the amplicon by following the gel extraction protocol as per kit manual.
Use an equal amount of the PCR products from Reactions 1 and 2 with primers Fwd BamH1-SCO1 and Rev TOMM20-His-EcoRI.
Follow Phusion Hot Start II High-Fidelity PCR Master Mix protocol at 68°C for annealing.
Separate the samples on a 1% agarose gel after PCR amplification.
Observe relevant DNA bands under a transilluminator.
Cut the 468-bp fragment from the gel.
Purify the amplicon by following the gel extraction protocol as per kit manual.
Digest the PCR product from Reaction 3 using BamHI and EcoRI restriction enzymes.
Purify the digested fragment using the QIAquick gel extraction kit per manufacturer’s protocol.
Determine the purity and concentration of the purified MitoT DNA fragment using a UV-Vis spectrophotometer.
Amplify and digest the pcDNA3-eGFP vector according to standard protocols.
Transform E. coli DH5α competent cells with the pcDNA3-eGFP plasmid as per standard protocol.
Inoculate a single colony in 5 mL of LB media containing ampicillin and incubate for 8 h at 37°C.
Take 100 μL of grown starter culture and inoculate it into 100 mL of LB media containing ampicillin.
Pellet the cells by centrifuging at 5,000 g for 15 min at room temperature (20°C–22°C).
Isolate the plasmid using a plasmid midi prep endotoxin-free kit per manufacturer’s instructions.
Quantitate plasmid concentration using a UV-Vis spectrophotometer.
Digest the plasmid using BamHI and EcoRI restriction enzymes according to standard NEB digestion protocol.
Separate the digested plasmid on a 1% agarose gel, cut out the desired band.
Purify the cut-out band using a gel purification kit.
Determine the purity and concentration of the purified digested plasmid using a UV-Vis spectrophotometer.
Set up ligation reaction (Figure 1B).
Incubate for 1 h in a thermal cycler at 16°C.
Transform 5 μL of ligation mix into E. coli DH5α competent cells.
Select single colonies and inoculate in 5 mL LB containing ampicillin in a glass tube.
Incubate the tubes for 16 hours at 37°C.
Centrifuge the tubes at 5,000 g for 15 min at room temperature (20°C–22°C) to pellet cells.
Isolate plasmid from pelleted cells for analysis.
Digest isolated plasmid with EcoRI and BamHI restriction enzymes.
Electrophoretically separate the digest on a 1% agarose gel to confirm the presence of the MitoT insert (468-bp band).
Validate the sequence of the MitoT construct by DNA sequencing.
Inoculate 5 mL of LB-Ampicillin medium with an E. coli clone harboring confirmed MitoT plasmid.
Incubate for 8 hours at 37°C to measure the OD600 of the initial inoculum.
Inoculate 100 μL in 100 mL LB medium containing ampicillin antibiotic.
Centrifuge the culture at 5,000 g for 15 min at room temperature (20°C–22°C) to pellet cells.
Isolate plasmid using a midiprep endotoxin-free plasmid purification kit per manufacturer’s instructions.
Determine the purity and concentration of isolated plasmid using a UV-Vis spectrophotometer.
Seed 5 × 10^5 cells per well into a 6-well plate or 35 mm dish twenty-four hours prior to transfection.
Transfect the cells with 1 μg of control vector pcDNA3-eGFP and pcDNA3-MitoT-eGFP plasmid using Lipofectamine 3000 transfection reagent.
Change the media after 16 h of transfection.
At 48 hours post-transfection, start the selection of G418-resistant clones using 2 mg/mL of G418.
Determine an individual effective concentration of G418 for every cell line used by making a titration curve.
Keep cells under antibiotic pressure for at least 7 days, replacing medium every 2 days.
Confirm expression and establishment of a MitoT-expressing stable cell line by fluorescence microscopy or western blotting using anti-GFP antibody.
Harvest the cells and make a cell suspension with approximately 5 × 10^6 cells per mL.
Sort MitoT-GFP-positive cells using a 488-nm laser with a 530/30 bandpass filter.
Use non-transfected cells to determine proper threshold gate for eGFP-negative cells.
Sort the cells in 10% FBS-containing DMEM medium containing 20 mM HEPES, pH 7.4.
Analyze isolated cells under a fluorescence microscope to confirm proper subcellular localization of the eGFP signal.
Centrifuge cells at 300 g for 10 min at room temperature (20°C–22°C).
Remove the medium and transfer the cells to the 10% FBS-containing DMEM medium containing 2 mg/mL of G418.
Re-seed the FACS-sorted GFP positive cells in a 6-well plate.
Add 10% FBS-containing DMEM medium with 2 mg/mL G418 antibiotic.
Change the medium every other day.
Culture for 7 days under antibiotic selection pressure.
Check for eGFP signal presence under a fluorescence microscope.
Trypsinize and re-seed surviving cells into a fresh 6-well plate.
Allow cells to grow to 90% confluency.
Cryofreeze some of the cells for future use.
Seed the cells into glass-bottom 35-mm dishes.
Prepare a fresh 1 mM stock solution of MitoTracker DeepRed dye in DMSO.
Store the 1 mM MitoTracker DeepRed dye solution at -20°C.
Dilute the dye at a 1:1000 dilution (final working concentration 1 μM) in FluoroBrite DMEM medium.
Remove the culture medium and wash the cells once with 1 mL of 1× PBS.
Add 1 mL of MitoTracker dye-containing medium to the 35-mm dish.
Incubate for 30 min at 37°C.
Remove medium from cells.
Wash cells twice with 1 mL FluoroBrite DMEM medium.
Add 1 mL of FluoroBright DMEM medium containing 1:2000 diluted Hoechst 33342 (final working concentration 5 μg/mL).
Incubate for 10 min in the dark.
Wash cells twice with FluoroBright DMEM medium.
Add 1 mL of FluoroBrite DMEM medium supplemented with 1% FBS.
Observe cells using a 60× oil objective.
Use ultraviolet 405 nm solid state laser for Hoechst 33342 excitation.
Use 425–475 nm bandpass filter for Hoechst 33342 emission.
Focus the cells according to optimal nuclear staining signal.
Observe eGFP signal using a 488 nm solid state excitation laser.
Use 500–550 nm bandpass filter for eGFP emission.
For MitoTracker DeepRed imaging, use 640 nm solid state excitation laser.
Use 633–673 nm emission filter for MitoTracker DeepRed.
Grow cell lines in a 30-mm culture dish overnight (∼12–16 h).
Treat cells with 2 μM carbonyl cyanide m-chlorophenyl hydrazone (CCCP) or mock control for 1 h at 37°C in CO2 incubator.
Transthyretin the cells and wash three times with 500 μL PBS.
Count cells using an automated cell counter.
Pellet 1 million cells for each cell line being analyzed.
Fix cells with 2.5% glutaraldehyde (prepared in TEM wash buffer) for 1 h at room temperature.
Keep fixed cells overnight (∼12–16 h) at 4°C.
Wash the cells with 500 μL TEM wash buffer three times, 5 min each at 500 g.
Pellet the cells and embed in 1% low-melting agarose.
Add 250 μL lukewarm agarose to the cell pellets.
Vortex to resuspend and centrifuge at 9,500 g at room temperature (20°C–22°C) for 5 min.
Allow agarose to solidify at 4°C for 3–4 h.
Transfer agarose to a Petri dish using small spoon-scoop spatula and filter forceps.
Cut out a 2-mm block of solidified agarose containing the cell pellet.
Post-fix the cells with 1% osmium tetroxide in deionized water for 1 h.
Wash the cells with 500 μL deionized water three times for 5 min each time.
Gradually dehydrate agarose block with embedded cells by washing it with 50%, 75%, and 95% ethanol (5 min each wash).
Incubate in pure Spurr’s solution for 2–3 h at room temperature (20°C–22°C).
Keep the cell block in a double-end mold and incubate in 1:1 solution of 100% ethanol/Spurr’s solution for 2 h at room temperature (20°C–22°C).
Incubate in pure Spurr’s solution for 24–36 h at 60°C in a vacuum oven.
Remove the dried block and trim the edges.
Cut 70–90 nm-thick sections using a Leica UC7 ultramicrotome.
Place the sections on EM grids.
Stain with 1% uranyl acetate for 10 minutes.
Rinse thoroughly up to 10 times with double distilled water.
Stain sections with 1% lead citrate for 5 minutes.
Spot 100 μL of ddH2O at 8 places on a Petri dish and dip grid 10 times into each spot for washing.
Image at 10,000× magnification with a Hitachi H7500 transmission electron microscope at 80 kV setting.
Image at 25,000× magnification with a Hitachi H7500 transmission electron microscope at 80 kV setting.
Take 25–30 images for each section.
Remove media from cells.
Wash the cells with 5 mL of 1× PBS.
Harvest 20 million MitoT-eGFP expressing MEF cells by scraping.
Pellet down cells at 800 g for 5 min at room temperature (20°C–22°C).
Remove supernatant.
Resuspend cells in 2 ml pre-chilled MTE buffer per 10 million cells, adding 10 μL of 0.2 M PMSF per mL of MTE buffer just before use.
Sonicate for 10 s at 20%–30% amplitude.
Keep samples on ice for 20 s.
Centrifuge at 2,000 g for 10 min at 4°C.
Recover the supernatant and transfer to a new tube.
Centrifuge recovered supernatant at 12,000 g for 10 min at 4°C.
Add 500 μL of MTE buffer containing 0.2 M PMSF to the crude mitochondria fraction.
Resuspend the pellet and aliquot in 50 μl fractions.
Determine total protein concentration of mitochondria-enriched fraction using Coomassie (Bradford) Protein Assay kit.
Flash-freeze crude mitochondrial fractions in liquid nitrogen and store aliquots at -80°C for later use.
Take 100 μg of mitochondria, pellet the organelles at 12,000 g for 10 min at 4°C, and resuspend pelleted mitochondria in 0.5 mL of 0.1 M alkaline sodium bicarbonate solution, pH 7.5 or 11.5.
Use 0.5 mL of ultrapure water for mock-treatment sample.
Vortex the samples.
Incubate samples on ice for 30 min.
Transfer samples into 5 mL polycarbonate tubes and adjust volume to 3 mL with 0.1 M sodium bicarbonate or ultrapure water.
Ultracentrifuge at 175,000 g for 30 min at 4°C.
Keep obtained pellets on ice for further steps.
Take supernatant fraction into a fresh 1.5 mL tubes and precipitate protein using 20% TCA and 0.07% (w/v) sodium deoxycholate.
Incubate these samples on ice for 45 min.
Centrifuge at 16,000 g for 10 min at 4°C.
Wash the pellet with ice-cold acetone and centrifuge at 16,000 g for 2 min at 4°C.
Repeat washing step two times.
Air dry the pellet after final wash.
Resuspend pellets obtained from step ‘c’ and step ‘d’ in 10 μL of 0.1M NaOH.
Perform standard SDS-PAGE and immunoblotting with relevant antibodies.
